weights.csoNote: THE default hypothesis for this complaint in Uganda, not a 'don't forget' — hence the only basePrior 4 in the file alongside HIV. COUGH IS SUPPORTING ONLY AND ITS ABSENCE CARRIES NO NEGATIVE WEIGHT: a large share of TB here is smear-negative, extrapulmonary or disseminated (36% of HIV-infected Ugandan inpatients with NEGATIVE sputum smears still had culture-positive pulmonary TB), so wasting with no respiratory symptom is a routine presentation and chest-centric Western teaching misleads. Do NOT use a normal BMI to rule out — 51% of confirmed pulmonary TB in Kampala had normal weight. Male prior is +1 not +2: the 4.1 male:female PREVALENCE ratio is a burden ratio, not an odds ratio among symptomatic weight-loss presenters, and female absolute prevalence remains very high. Ugandan age bands were not sourced, so agePrior is deliberately empty rather than importing a Western curve. EXPECT CO-DIAGNOSIS: 73% of hospitalised Ugandan adults with advanced HIV had >=2 aetiologies — finding TB does not close HIV, lymphoma or the rest.
weights.weightCitation: Uganda National Tuberculosis Prevalence Survey 2014-2015 (adult prevalence 401/100,000; males 734 vs females 178) — the primary national denominator; WHO AFRO Uganda TB burden (~91,000 cases/year, 32% HIV-coinfected); Law et al., National tuberculosis prevalence surveys in Africa 2008-2016, Trop Med Int Health 2020 (Uganda male:female 4.1, highest in Africa); 'Clinical and Radiographic Factors Do Not Accurately Diagnose Smear-Negative Tuberculosis in HIV-infected Inpatients in Uganda', PLOS One 2010 (72/202 = 36%); WHO four-symptom TB screen (cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss).

weights.csoNote: HIV/AIDS was the single leading cause of medical admission at Mulago (30% of ~50,000 admissions over four years, ahead of hypertension 14%, TB 13.1%), with 25% case fatality — it does not appear in a Western weight-loss differential at all, and here it is joint-commonest. Weight loss is not merely associated, it is the STAGING CRITERION: WHO stage 3 requires unexplained severe weight loss >10%, stage 4 defines HIV wasting syndrome. BEING ON ART DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT — 62% of hospitalised Ugandan adults with advanced HIV disease were ART-experienced (median 28 months on therapy), so a 'known HIV, on ART' history must never down-weight this entry. sexPrior deliberately NEUTRAL: community prevalence favours women (7.2% vs 4.3%) while hospitalised advanced disease is 55% male — the two effects oppose and inventing a prior would be unsourced. Consider unmasking TB-IRIS in anyone recently started on ART; the EMR has no ART-status field, so no ART-conditional scoring is encoded.
weights.weightCitation: Kalyesubula et al., 'Trends of admissions and case fatality rates among medical in-patients at a tertiary hospital in Uganda', PLOS One 2019;14(5):e0216060; WHO clinical staging of HIV disease in adults (stage 3 >10% weight loss; stage 4 HIV wasting syndrome); Tugume L, Semitala FC, Owachi D, Kagimu E, Kamya MR, Meya DB, 'Clinical characteristics and morbidity among hospitalized adults with advanced HIV disease in Uganda during test and treat era', PLOS Glob Public Health 2023;3(10):e0002457; UPHIA 2020-21 (adult prevalence 5.5%, women 7.1% / men 3.8%).

weights.csoNote: THIS ENTRY IS THE SOLID-ORGAN / OLDER-ADULT NODE ONLY. The HIV-associated cancers (Kaposi sarcoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma) peak in the early-to-mid thirties in Kampala and would be actively HARMED by the age prior here, so they are carried as a SEPARATE entry — one node cannot hold both age curves, and encoding a single -2 under 40 would hide the commonest malignancies in this population. The under-40 delta is therefore only -1, not the -2 the Western data would suggest: cancer probability rises steeply with age (NICE NG12 evidence review: 50-59 = 2.15%, 60-69 = 4.82%, 70-79 = 7.17%), but the youngest-band figures could not be independently corroborated and Uganda's cancer mix is younger than the UK's. Kampala incidence is also RISING (prostate ~+100%, breast ~+70%, cervix ~+45% over 1991-2015), so do not treat malignancy as a Western-only concern.
weights.weightCitation: NICE NG12 suspected cancer recognition and referral, evidence review age-band cancer probabilities (50-59 = 2.15%, 60-69 = 4.82%, 70-79 = 7.17%); Nicholson BD et al., 'The internal validation of weight and weight change coding using weight measurement data within the UK primary care Electronic Health Record', Br J Gen Pract 2018;68(670):e311 (25 studies, >11.5m patients); Bosch X, Monclús E, Escoda O et al., 'Unintentional weight loss: Clinical characteristics and outcomes in a prospective cohort of 2677 patients', PLOS One 2017;12(4):e0175125 (malignancy 33%); Bukirwa et al., 'Trends in the incidence of cancer in Kampala, Uganda, 1991 to 2015', Int J Cancer 2021; AAFP, 'Unintentional Weight Loss in Older Adults', Am Fam Physician 2021;104(1):34-40 (malignancy 19-36%).

weights.csoNote: THE CLASSIC DISCRIMINATOR OF THIS COMPLAINT: weight loss DESPITE eating well. 'Good appetite' carries the heaviest weight here and is the single most useful thing the clerkship captures for this entry — see the file-level note on the appetite bridge. Female predominance of thyrotoxicosis is well established internationally; Ugandan-specific incidence was not sourced beyond a 1974 hospital series in which goitre dominated, so basePrior 1 is conservative and needs CSO calibration. NOTE the overlap trap: heat intolerance and tremor also occur in TB and in advanced HIV, and hyperthyroidism is far rarer than either here — this entry should support, not displace, the infective hypotheses.
weights.weightCitation: ATA Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism and Other Causes of Thyrotoxicosis (Ross et al., Thyroid 2016); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), thyrotoxicosis; 'Thyroid disease in Uganda' (PMID 4439461, 1974) — five-year Ugandan hospital series, goitre-predominant; AAFP, Am Fam Physician 2021;104(1):34-40 (endocrine causes of unintentional weight loss).

weights.csoNote: TWO PROBLEMS THE CSO SHOULD RULE ON. (1) NAMING: the approved name is 'New diabetes mellitus', but its risk token 'diabetes mellitus' fires on ALREADY-DIAGNOSED diabetes through the existing alias to the PMH screen key — i.e. a known diabetic scores a new-diagnosis hypothesis. Rather than silently drop the token (which would blind the entry to the very common uncontrolled-diabetic wasting presentation), it is held at a deliberately LOW +1 while 'Polyuria / polydipsia' at +4 does the real work. RECOMMEND RENAMING to 'Diabetes mellitus — new or uncontrolled' in a future approved-map revision; the rename cannot be done from a weights file because entries match the map by exact name. (2) GLUCOSE NOW RANKS (ADR 0078): 'random glucose over 11.1' is derived from recorded vitals and carries +4 here — it is the actual diagnostic discriminator, so this entry no longer depends on the known-diabetes token to surface. FINDING DIABETES DOES NOT CLOSE THE CASE: diabetes roughly triples TB risk and the two co-present constantly here; NICE NG12 also treats new-onset diabetes as a pancreatic-cancer flag.
weights.weightCitation: WHO/ADA diagnostic criteria for diabetes mellitus (fasting >=7.0 mmol/L; random >=11.1 mmol/L with symptoms); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (diabetes); NICE NG12 1.2.5 (new-onset diabetes with weight loss as a pancreatic-cancer referral trigger); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022).

weights.csoNote: sexPrior deliberately NEUTRAL, against the Western default. The Ugandan national meta-analysis (127 studies, 123,859 individuals, pooled depression prevalence 30.2%) does not establish the female excess that UK/US sources assume, and its meta-regression runs directionally against it — so no sex prior is encoded rather than importing one. Negative weights on fever, night sweats and lymphadenopathy are the safety mechanism: this is the entry most likely to prematurely close a wasting work-up in a young patient, and it must fall away the moment an infective or malignant feature appears. Depression and TB/HIV frequently COEXIST here; ranking depression highly must never be read as excluding them. CALIBRATION: fever, night sweats and lymphadenopathy are weighted -3 rather than -2 because at -2 a patient with poor appetite, low mood, fever AND night sweats still scored exactly on the Leading threshold — a depressed-looking presentation with two infective red flags must not lead.
weights.weightCitation: Uganda national depression meta-analysis (127 studies, 123,859 individuals; pooled prevalence 30.2%, 95% CI 26.7-34.1), PLOS One 2022;17(10):e0276552; AAFP, 'Unintentional Weight Loss in Older Adults', Am Fam Physician 2021;104(1):34-40 (psychiatric causes 9-42%); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022).

weights.csoNote: CARRIED SEPARATELY FROM 'Malignancy' BECAUSE THE AGE CURVE IS OPPOSITE. Kaposi sarcoma is the commonest male cancer in Kampala (18/100,000) and, with non-Hodgkin lymphoma, peaks in the early-to-mid thirties — exactly where the solid-organ entry's age prior pushes DOWN. THE SPECIFIC LOCAL ERROR THIS PREVENTS: HIV-associated lymphoma is repeatedly misdiagnosed and treated as tuberculosis, because both give fever, night sweats, wasting and lymphadenopathy in a young person with HIV. The rule this entry encodes: persistent wasting with lymphadenopathy that does NOT respond to anti-TB therapy means BIOPSY, not a second course of TB treatment. Conditional pin (HIV/immunosuppression, or lymphadenopathy) so it does not fire on every wasting patient. Feature weights are set on clinical grounds — the specific '91% of NHL presented with lymphadenopathy' figure quoted in sourcing could not be independently verified and is deliberately NOT cited here.
weights.weightCitation: Buyego P et al., 'Possible misdiagnosis of HIV associated lymphoma as tuberculosis among patients attending Uganda Cancer Institute', AIDS Res Ther 2017;14:13 (183 charts; 57.9% male; median age 35, IQR 28-45); Kampala Cancer Registry 2009-2013 (8,168 cases; Kaposi sarcoma 18/100,000, highest male incidence); WHO clinical staging of HIV disease (KS and lymphoma as stage 4 conditions).

weights.csoNote: THE OMISSION THIS FILE EXISTS TO FIX. Subacute infective endocarditis presenting as weeks of fever, night sweats and unintentional weight loss in a young adult with rheumatic valve disease is a mainstream Ugandan presentation, it is CURABLE, and it was absent from the approved map — while chronic heart failure, drawn from the same rheumatic-heart-disease literature, was proposed twice. IE was present in 8.2% of newly diagnosed RHD patients at Mulago. It is also FULLY REACHABLE with capture that already exists: 'cardiac murmur' is derived by the structured cardiovascular exam, and Janeway lesions, Osler's nodes, splinter haemorrhages and splenomegaly are existing exam chips — no new tokens required. Conditional pin on a murmur or a peripheral stigma or a valve risk, so it stays silent in the many wasting patients with a normal heart. Blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics; echocardiography.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2023 Guidelines for the management of endocarditis (modified Duke criteria; blood cultures before antibiotics); World Heart Federation criteria for echocardiographic diagnosis of rheumatic heart disease; Mulago rheumatic heart disease cohort (infective endocarditis in 8.2% of newly diagnosed RHD patients); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), infective endocarditis.

weights.csoNote: The only entry proposed independently by two sourcing lenses. Chronic diarrhoea lasting over one month is itself a WHO stage 3 HIV criterion and part of the stage 4 wasting-syndrome definition, so this overlaps HIV/AIDS by design rather than by accident — cryptosporidiosis, cystoisosporiasis and microsporidiosis at low CD4 are the documented Ugandan causes, and abdominal TB belongs in the same bracket. basePrior 2 is inferred from disease prevalence, NOT measured against a weight-loss denominator; flagged for CSO calibration. Steatorrhoea and the classic malabsorption discriminators have no capture token today.
weights.weightCitation: WHO clinical staging of HIV disease in adults (unexplained chronic diarrhoea >1 month = stage 3; HIV wasting syndrome = stage 4); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (chronic diarrhoea, opportunistic infections); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), malabsorption.

weights.csoNote: The map had NO hepatic entry despite two dominant Ugandan drivers: hepatitis B is highly endemic (4.3% national HBsAg, ~19% north-west, ~25% north-east regionally) and Uganda has the highest per-capita alcohol consumption in Africa (12.21 L pure alcohol/year vs 6.3 L African and 6.18 L global average; 19.93 L among men). Both routes end in cirrhosis with sarcopenia and anorexia, and hepatitis B additionally drives hepatocellular carcinoma — so a high score here should also raise the malignancy question rather than settle it. Alcohol is carried as a RISK token here rather than as a separate 'alcohol use disorder' entry, because the clerkship has no social-history or units-per-week capture and a standalone entry would rank on almost nothing. basePrior inferred from disease prevalence, not from a weight-loss denominator.
weights.weightCitation: WHO hepatitis B fact sheet and Uganda hepatitis B seroprevalence surveys (4.3% national HBsAg; higher in northern regions); WHO World Health Statistics 2023 (Uganda per-capita alcohol consumption 12.21 L, highest in Africa); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (chronic liver disease, hepatitis B); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), cirrhosis.

weights.csoNote: Uraemic anorexia is a genuine and under-recognised cause of wasting here. CKD prevalence is 2-7% nationally (12.5% in eastern Uganda, up to ~15% in HIV and hypertension), it is one of the fastest-rising shares of Mulago medical admissions (annual percentage change +24%), and protein-energy wasting was present in 47.3% (44/93, 95% CI 37.2-57.5) of Mulago CKD patients. NOTE: the 47.3% figure corrects a transcription error in sourcing, where the numerator 44 was misread as a percentage — the true prevalence is higher, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for this entry. basePrior inferred from disease prevalence, not a weight-loss denominator.
weights.weightCitation: Protein-energy wasting in Ugandan CKD patients, BMC Nephrology 2018 (PMC6003131) — 44/93 CKD patients = 47.3% (95% CI 37.2-57.5); Kalyesubula et al., PLOS One 2019;14(5):e0216060 (CKD annual percentage change +24% of Mulago medical admissions); KDIGO CKD guideline; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023.

weights.dx: Post-TB lung disease (including chronic pulmonary aspergillosis)
weights.csoNote: STRICTLY conditional on previously-treated TB PLUS a persisting respiratory feature — silent otherwise. THE SPECIFIC ERROR IT PREVENTS: a patient who completed TB treatment returns wasting, coughing and haemoptysing, and is given a SECOND empirical course of anti-TB therapy when the actual diagnosis is chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (19.8% of Ugandan pulmonary TB patients with persisting symptoms, >25% one-year mortality) or post-TB obstructive lung disease (23% COPD prevalence among cured Ugandan drug-resistant TB patients). CPA is merged with post-TB lung disease into ONE entry rather than carried as a standalone zebra, because they share the gate, the population and the action: image the chest and send Aspergillus serology before re-treating for TB.
weights.weightCitation: Namusobya et al., 'Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis in patients with active pulmonary tuberculosis with persisting symptoms in Uganda', Mycoses 2022 (32/162 = 19.8%, Mulago); post-TB chronic lung disease in Ugandan drug-resistant TB survivors (COPD 23%); Denning et al., chronic pulmonary aspergillosis diagnostic and management guideline (ESCMID/ERS).

weights.csoNote: CHEAP TO TREAT, FATAL IF MISSED (adrenal crisis) — but deliberately basePrior 0 and STRICTLY pinned on TB or HIV, because an unconditional pin at this rarity would alarm-flood the complaint. Specifically Ugandan: in sub-Saharan Africa the dominant causes of primary adrenal insufficiency are ADRENAL TB and HIV rather than autoimmunity, and pooled prevalence is 26% (95% CI 12-40%) in African TB patients. IMPORTANT SAFETY CAVEAT ON THE EXAM SIGN: hyperpigmentation is the textbook rule-in, but it is genuinely hard to read in very dark skin, and the clerkship offers only a single generic 'pigmentation' skin chip with no site specificity. It is therefore weighted +2, NOT the +4 the textbooks would imply — the pin does not depend on it. RECOMMEND adding site-specific chips (buccal/gingival, palmar-crease, scar pigmentation) and, once vitals are indexed, gating additionally on hypotension.
weights.weightCitation: Kibirige D et al., 'Prevalence and Predictors of Adrenal Insufficiency in Adults With Tuberculosis or HIV', Open Forum Infect Dis 2024;11(4):ofae098 (Africa TB subgroup 26%, 95% CI 12-40%); Merck Manual Professional, Addison disease (hyperpigmentation may be more difficult to detect in darker skin); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), adrenal insufficiency.

weights.dx: Inadequate intake (food insecurity, dysphagia, dementia, dentition)
weights.csoNote: DELIBERATELY BROADER THAN 'POVERTY'. Framed only as food insecurity it would miss the mechanical and neurological causes that matter just as much on a Ugandan medical ward — post-stroke dysphagia, dementia, and dentition. Adult underweight prevalence in northern Uganda is 22.3% (men) / 16.0% (women), so the socioeconomic route is real, but it must not become the lazy answer. STRONG NEGATIVE WEIGHTS ARE THE SAFETY MECHANISM: this entry must collapse the instant fever, night sweats, lymphadenopathy or haemoptysis appears, and it must never outrank Tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS or either malignancy entry when their features are present — attributing wasting to poverty in a patient with undiagnosed TB is the exact harm this design guards against. CAPTURE GAPS: no dysphagia token, no dentition assessment, no social or food-security history; the entry currently rides appetite plus the cognitive/stroke proxies only.
weights.weightCitation: Uganda Demographic and Health Survey / northern Uganda adult undernutrition (underweight 22.3% men, 16.0% women); AAFP, 'Unintentional Weight Loss in Older Adults', Am Fam Physician 2021;104(1):34-40 (social factors, isolation and financial constraints as contributors); Wallace JI, Schwartz RS, LaCroix AZ et al., J Am Geriatr Soc 1995;43:329-37 (PMID 7706619).

weights.csoNote: Cardiac cachexia is a real but late cause of wasting, hence less_likely at basePrior 1. Heart failure accounted for 9.3% of Mulago medical admissions, and Ugandan heart failure is a YOUNG-ADULT disease — cardiomyopathy (~40%) and rheumatic heart disease (~27%) rather than the ischaemic, elderly Western pattern — so no age prior is encoded. COPD was deliberately NOT bundled here (as one sourcing lens proposed): in this population post-TB obstructive disease is the dominant chronic airways problem and it lives in the post-TB lung disease entry, not as a smoking-driven Western sibling. If a murmur is present, INFECTIVE ENDOCARDITIS must be considered before settling on heart failure. basePrior inferred from disease prevalence, not a weight-loss denominator.
weights.weightCitation: Kalyesubula et al., PLOS One 2019;14(5):e0216060 (heart failure 9.3% of Mulago medical admissions); Ugandan heart failure aetiology series (cardiomyopathy ~40%, rheumatic heart disease ~27% in young adults); ESC 2021 Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure; Fearon K et al., 'Definition and classification of cancer cachexia', Lancet Oncol 2011;12(5):489-495 (cachexia criteria).
